newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Thursday on the back of rises on the domestic A share markets in the past two days, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 10.50 percent from 10.00 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose sharply to 7.78 million lots from 2.97 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rises on the A share markets increased fund demand from major institutions, pushing up the rates and volumes today," one trader said.
Traders said the rates were likely to stay at the current levels on Friday with no market-moving news in sight.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on improved sentiment after rises in the past two weeks, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 rose slightly to 118.08 yuan from 118.02 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 933,071 lots from 1.51 million.
Traders expect the contracts to continue to rise in the short term with long-term investors seen building positions in the past few trading days.
